title: Homiliary
shelf_note: No tradition or collection assigned. These are 12th-century Caroline-minuscule homiliary leaves (Harvard) and a legitimate primary source.
structure_note: 6 leaves from different homilies: p2 is a sermon on the cross and the good thief (pencilled 'Sermo CLV, P.L. 39'), p4 is Augustine on John 13:31 (pencilled 'fer. V Palmarum, In Cena Domini'), and p5 is the homily on the feeding of the five thousand. Consistent with fragments of a homiliary, not a continuous book.

book_verdict: These are real 12th-century homiliary leaves, but flash-lite misreads the abbreviated Caroline minuscule throughout, and the fluent translation turns those misreadings into statements the homilies do not make: 'subdue it to the will of the flesh', 'the rock signified', 'things which were not written'. Not fit to show without a re-read.

title: Oratio ad immortalitatem illustriassimae nec non famigerratissimae laudis
shelf_note: No tradition or collection assigned. A 1562 manuscript oration praising the city of Lodi (Laus Pompeia), a civic humanist encomium unrelated to the library's core traditions.
structure_note: 52 pages, 52 with OCR but only 45 translated (7 untranslated, perhaps blanks or binding). Pencil foliation 4, 15, 26 on scans 14, 25, 36 runs consistently.
